lines.text: Nine is four plus five. Ten is one plus two plus three plus four.
lines.caption: Nine is four plus five. Ten is one plus two plus three plus four.

lines.text: But a few numbers can never be built this way. <short pause> Which ones?
lines.caption: But a few numbers can never be built this way. Which ones?

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's hunt down those stubborn numbers together.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's hunt down those stubborn numbers together.

lines.text: How many whole numbers, from one to fifty,
lines.caption: How many whole numbers, from one to fifty,

lines.text: can be written as the sum of two or more consecutive positive whole numbers?
lines.caption: can be written as the sum of two or more consecutive positive whole numbers?

lines.text: For example, nine is four plus five.
lines.caption: For example, nine is four plus five.

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look at them.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look at them.

lines.text: Consecutive means next to each other, with no gaps, like four, five and six.
lines.caption: Consecutive means next to each other, with no gaps, like four, five and six.

lines.text: We need at least two numbers in the run. Five on its own doesn't count.
lines.caption: We need at least two numbers in the run. Five on its own doesn't count.

lines.text: Every number in the run must be positive, so no zero and no negative numbers.
lines.caption: Every number in the run must be positive, so no zero and no negative numbers.

lines.text: So which numbers from one to fifty can we build, and how many are there?
lines.caption: So which numbers from one to fifty can we build, and how many are there?

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Let's make a list, one run length at a time, on a board from one to fifty.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Let's make a list, one run length at a time, on a board from one to fifty.

lines.text: Start with runs of two numbers. One plus two equals three. Two plus three equals five.
lines.caption: Start with runs of two numbers. One plus two equals three. Two plus three equals five.

lines.text: Two neighbors are one odd and one even, so their sum is always odd.
lines.caption: Two neighbors are one odd and one even, so their sum is always odd.

lines.text: That lights up every odd number from three to forty-nine. Twenty-four numbers already!
lines.caption: That lights up every odd number from three to forty-nine. Twenty-four numbers already!

lines.text: Runs of three make every multiple of three from six up: eight new even numbers.
lines.caption: Runs of three make every multiple of three from six up: eight new even numbers.

lines.text: Runs of four start at ten and go up by four each time. Eight more new cells!
lines.caption: Runs of four start at ten and go up by four each time. Eight more new cells!

lines.text: Runs of five go from fifteen up to fifty, but only twenty and forty are new.
lines.caption: Runs of five go from fifteen up to fifty, but only twenty and forty are new.

lines.text: Runs of six always add up to an odd number, so nothing new lights up.
lines.caption: Runs of six always add up to an odd number, so nothing new lights up.

lines.text: Next, runs of seven numbers. One through seven makes twenty-eight. That one is new!
lines.caption: Next, runs of seven numbers. One through seven makes twenty-eight. That one is new!

lines.text: Runs of eight: two through nine makes forty-four. Another new one!
lines.caption: Runs of eight: two through nine makes forty-four. Another new one!

lines.text: Runs of nine only make forty-five, and runs of ten start at fifty-five. Too big, so we stop.
lines.caption: Runs of nine only make forty-five, and runs of ten start at fifty-five. Too big, so we stop.

lines.text: Which cells are still dark? One, two, four, eight, sixteen and thirty-two.
lines.caption: Which cells are still dark? One, two, four, eight, sixteen and thirty-two.

lines.text: One and two are too small, since the smallest run is one plus two, which is three.
lines.caption: One and two are too small, since the smallest run is one plus two, which is three.

lines.text: So six numbers fail. Fifty minus six is forty-four!
lines.caption: So six numbers fail. Fifty minus six is forty-four!

lines.text: But WHY do those six numbers fail? Let's build runs out of blocks.
lines.caption: But WHY do those six numbers fail? Let's build runs out of blocks.

lines.text: Here's four plus five plus six, as three stacks of blocks.
lines.caption: Here's four plus five plus six, as three stacks of blocks.

lines.text: Move one block from the tallest stack to the shortest. Now every stack is five!
lines.caption: Move one block from the tallest stack to the shortest. Now every stack is five!

lines.text: So a run with an odd length makes length times middle. Three times five is fifteen.
lines.caption: So a run with an odd length makes length times middle. Three times five is fifteen.

lines.text: Now an even run: two plus three plus four plus five.
lines.caption: Now an even run: two plus three plus four plus five.

lines.text: Pair the outside numbers, then the inside numbers. Each pair adds up to seven.
lines.caption: Pair the outside numbers, then the inside numbers. Each pair adds up to seven.

lines.text: Each pair has one odd number and one even number, so every pair sum is odd.
lines.caption: Each pair has one odd number and one even number, so every pair sum is odd.

lines.text: So this total is two pairs times seven, which makes fourteen.
lines.caption: So this total is two pairs times seven, which makes fourteen.

lines.text: Either way, the total has an odd factor bigger than one: the length, or the pair sum.
lines.caption: Either way, the total has an odd factor bigger than one: the length, or the pair sum.

lines.text: Now look at our six numbers. They're all powers of two.
lines.caption: Now look at our six numbers. They're all powers of two.

lines.text: Split them into factors, and you only ever find twos. There's no odd factor at all!
lines.caption: Split them into factors, and you only ever find twos. There's no odd factor at all!

lines.text: So no run of numbers can ever make a power of two.
lines.caption: So no run of numbers can ever make a power of two.

lines.text: Every other number does have an odd factor, and we can use it to build a run.
lines.caption: Every other number does have an odd factor, and we can use it to build a run.

lines.text: Eighteen is three times six. So take three numbers around six: five, six and seven.
lines.caption: Eighteen is three times six. So take three numbers around six: five, six and seven.

lines.text: Forty-four is four times eleven. But eleven numbers around four would go below one.
lines.caption: Forty-four is four times eleven. But eleven numbers around four would go below one.

lines.text: So use eleven as the pair sum instead: four pairs that each add up to eleven.
lines.caption: So use eleven as the pair sum instead: four pairs that each add up to eleven.

lines.text: Two plus nine, three plus eight, four plus seven, five plus six. That's two through nine!
lines.caption: Two plus nine, three plus eight, four plus seven, five plus six. That's two through nine!

lines.text: So the powers of two are the only numbers that fail, and the answer is forty-four again.
lines.caption: So the powers of two are the only numbers that fail, and the answer is forty-four again.

lines.text: Twenty-four only counts runs of two, the odd numbers. It forgot even ones like six and ten.
lines.caption: Twenty-four only counts runs of two, the odd numbers. It forgot even ones like six and ten.

lines.text: Forty-three crosses out seven powers of two, but sixty-four is past fifty!
lines.caption: Forty-three crosses out seven powers of two, but sixty-four is past fifty!

lines.text: Forty-five forgets that one can't be built. One is just one, all by itself.
lines.caption: Forty-five forgets that one can't be built. One is just one, all by itself.

lines.text: Forty-seven crosses out only one, two and four. But eight, sixteen and thirty-two fail too.
lines.caption: Forty-seven crosses out only one, two and four. But eight, sixteen and thirty-two fail too.

lines.text: Great habit: check until the runs get too big, and check each power of two is really in range.
lines.caption: Great habit: check until the runs get too big, and check each power of two is really in range.

scenes.chapter: Your turn: one to one hundred

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Same question, but now from one to one hundred.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Same question, but now from one to one hundred.

lines.text: Use the rule. Hunt for the numbers that fail first.
lines.caption: Use the rule. Hunt for the numbers that fail first.

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

scenes.chapter: One to one hundred: the answer

lines.text: Let's check. The numbers that fail are the powers of two.
lines.caption: Let's check. The numbers that fail are the powers of two.

lines.text: One, two, four, eight, sixteen, thirty-two, and now sixty-four joins them.
lines.caption: One, two, four, eight, sixteen, thirty-two, and now sixty-four joins them.

lines.text: The next power, one hundred twenty-eight, is past one hundred, so we stop there.
lines.caption: The next power, one hundred twenty-eight, is past one hundred, so we stop there.

lines.text: That's seven numbers that fail. One hundred minus seven is ninety-three!
lines.caption: That's seven numbers that fail. One hundred minus seven is ninety-three!

lines.text: Quick check: one hundred is five times twenty, so eighteen through twenty-two works.
lines.caption: Quick check: one hundred is five times twenty, so eighteen through twenty-two works.

lines.text: A run of two or more consecutive numbers always has an odd factor bigger than one.
lines.caption: A run of two or more consecutive numbers always has an odd factor bigger than one.

lines.text: So only the powers of two can't be built, even in a huge range. Find them, and take them away.
lines.caption: So only the powers of two can't be built, even in a huge range. Find them, and take them away.

lines.text: I'm Vantee! Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee! Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
